COMMERCIAL BLOCKER - multi-seat customers rate-limited themselves into a degraded UI. resolveIp() reads cf-connecting-ip, which for a company is the shared NAT/VPN egress: every seat presents the SAME ip. The IP bucket is 100/60s, TEN TIMES TIGHTER than the per-user bucket (1,000/60s), and it was evaluated FIRST and unconditionally, so an authenticated user could never reach their own allowance. One authenticated page load costs a measured floor of 15 requests - roughly SIX PAGE LOADS PER MINUTE FOR AN ENTIRE OFFICE; a ten-seat customer exhausts it on the 9am wave. The client has ZERO 429 handling (0 occurrences of '429' in wired/live-data.js), so it surfaces as a silent, causeless 'unavailable'. FIX: the IP bucket now governs UNAUTHED traffic only, which is what its own comment already claimed ('covers unauthed paths'). Layering is preserved, not removed - unauthed keeps the tight 100/60s, authed stays capped per user (1,000) and per tenant (5,000), both already correctly sized. Raising the IP limit was rejected: it keeps a shared-NAT ceiling that punishes large customers for being large.
